title: Type Aliases
concept: Use type to create an alias — a new name for an existing type that adds meaning and clarity.
why: Type aliases make code self-documenting. Age is clearer than Int; Meters is clearer than Float64.
tips: Aliases add SEMANTIC meaning — they tell you WHAT the Int represents
Aliases don't create new types — `Age` is still just an `Int` at runtime
common_mistakes: Creating aliases that don't add meaning: `type Int2 = Int` is useless
Thinking aliases prevent mixing: `Meters` and `Feet` can still be added
Using `snake_case` for type names — types use `PascalCase` in XIOM
